main_body: Tall townhouse: a slate mansard roof with two dormers and a chimney, an orange cornice, a red-brick facade with four lit windows per floor, a balcony rail, and a striped awning over a shopfront.
top_band: At x=32, rows 17-22 form a light grey-blue roof-top band (L=122 edge row, then L=95). It ends in a light front-edge line at row 23 (L=122) and a dark row 24 (L=53). Below that, slate roof slope in rows 25-43 steps from L=103 to L=79 to L=51. The orange cornice follows in rows 44-46.
evidence: The roof is drawn as visible surfaces. A lighter flat top band (rows 17-22) closes with a distinct light edge row (23) and a dark shadow row (24). Under it is a large sloped slate surface (rows 25-43) with dormers, then a cornice. The brick facade below is the vertical south face and is very tall. The windows have light frames and sills, and the balcony and awning overhang with shading. This reads as roof surfaces above a front face rather than a plain elevation with a hat, so it passes the 3/4 contract. No receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: Structure and density are good. The median is 14 colours per tile, against 11 for the stone reference and 18 for h101. Flat-fill coverage is 2%. The slate scales, brick courses, window glazing and awning stripes carry several tones each. The weakness is the outline: 97% of dark edge pixels are neutral (#1d1722 and similar), against 7-9% on the references. That gives a uniform near-black sticker line round the silhouette, the roof band, the dormers and the chimney, where Beodeul uses a tinted dark tone of the adjacent material. The total of 54 distinct colours is also lower than the references, so it reads slightly flatter and more sticker-like beside them.
